same_key_policy: Match the exact Devanāgarī lemma or directive after removing whitespace, editorial double angle brackets, and Kāśikā parenthetical gaṇasūtra numbers. Preserve every primary position, diacritic, consonant, vowel and source-only spelling. No fuzzy or reconstructed identity earns an exact match.

directives.source_decision: eṣaṇī as the instrument with which one searches; a locus has a different ṅīp route.
The Nyāsa gives sumaṅgalā outside the naming condition; it preserves an alternative source of ī for a proper name.
The Nyāsa contrasts rohitā outside the stellar designation.
A nonstellar a-stem analysis gives revatā. The matup analysis can produce nonstellar revatī with ṅīp, distinguished from ṅīṣ by accent.
The Nyāsa writes kaṭī for the hip and contrasts kaṭā outside this lexical designation.
The Nyāsa treats the words following this directive as the vṛttikāra’s examples. The Bālamanoramā reads gaurādi as an ākṛtigaṇa.

affix_ownership: 4.1.41 has two entry conditions, ṣ on a qualifying affix and lexical membership in gaurādi. Nartakī illustrates the former and naṭī can be derived using a member naṭa. The two are different input stems.
Matup can yield ṅīp in nonstellar revatī. An unaccented final ī cannot identify the source suffix.
With pippalyādi the textual layer of the examples matters. An ākṛtigaṇa permits grammarians to recognize suitable additional examples; absence from one enumerated list is not a universal rejection.
projection: Select source, governing rule and its local gaṇa, source position, meaning and accent path before forming ī. The source with index 231 is headed gaurādi under 6.2.194; that shared heading alone supplies no feminine entitlement. A membership map keyed only by name loses its governing rule.
